items.correctExplanation: Right — the reply mugs the researcher instead of the research. Credentials never settle data.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is ad hominem. The dropout jibe dodges the study; only evidence answers evidence.
items.lessonContent:
Ad hominem mugs messengers to dodge messages.
Credentials never settle data disputes.
Redirect every personal jab to the evidence.
Share this: defend one claim purely on its data.
items.question: 'Ignore his climate study — he's a college dropout.' Name the flaw.
items.title: The Dropout Jibe

items.correctExplanation: Correct — nobody proposed banning cars; the reply torches an invented ban. Fight real proposals.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is strawman. The lane proposal became an invented car ban mid-reply.
items.lessonContent:
Strawmen torch proposals nobody made.
Quote opponents before refuting them.
Fictional extremes confess weak cases.
Share this: steel-man one rival view today.
items.question: 'A bike lane? So drivers should vanish entirely!' Name the trick.
items.title: The Vanishing Driver

items.correctExplanation: Yes — queues prove popularity, never quality. Crowds queue for fads too.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is bandwagon. A long line measures hype, not taste.
items.lessonContent:
Bandwagons sell queues as quality certificates.
Crowds err together with enthusiasm.
Taste with your own mouth first.
Share this: skip one hyped queue for a quiet gem.
items.question: 'This restaurant must be great — look at the queue!' Name the flaw.
items.title: The Hyped Queue

items.correctExplanation: Right — acting trophies confer no medical licenses. Badges work only in their field.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is appeal to authority. Fame in film prescribes nothing in pharmacies.
items.lessonContent:
Borrowed badges dazzle outside their jurisdiction.
Check the field printed on every expert.
Fame prescribes nothing, ever.
Share this: verify one endorser's real expertise.
items.question: 'This diet works — a movie star swears by it.' Name the borrow.
items.title: The Star Diet

items.correctExplanation: Correct — renting and buying never exhausted housing. The menu hides rooms full of options.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is false dilemma — renting isn't binary. Mortgages, co-ops, and waiting sit off the forced menu.
items.lessonContent:
False dilemmas print two-item menus for hundred-item worlds.
Always order off-menu: ask for option three.
Urgency enforces fake binaries.
Share this: add option three to one ultimatum.
items.question: 'Either buy now or rent forever' — which squeeze is this?
items.title: The Housing Squeeze

items.correctExplanation: Yes — each slide from sofas to ruin is asserted, never shown. Slopes need grip per step.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is slippery slope — naps don't chain. Daily naps don't lead to collapse without evidence per link.
items.lessonContent:
Slippery slopes assert avalanches without snow science.
Demand mechanisms at every step down.
Most slides stop two steps in.
Share this: halt one doomsday chain at step one.
items.question: 'Napping daily leads to laziness, then joblessness, then ruin' — which slide is this?
items.title: The Nap Avalanche

items.correctExplanation: Right — one rainy weekend can't convict a country. Samples of one prove nothing.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is hasty generalization. A weekend is no climate survey.
items.lessonContent:
Tiny samples shout the loudest nonsense.
Weekends never certify climates.
Ask sample size before accepting verdicts.
Share this: shrink one sweeping claim to its sample.
items.question: 'It rained all weekend — this country has no summer.' Name the leap.
items.title: The Rainy Verdict

items.correctExplanation: Correct — one neighbor's luck is not a trial. Stories illustrate; samples prove.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is anecdotal. A neighbor's fortune can't outweigh pharmacist statistics.
items.lessonContent:
Anecdotes are samples of one wearing tuxedos.
Neighbors' luck never outranks trials.
Counter stories with statistics kindly.
Share this: answer one anecdote with real numbers.
items.question: 'My neighbor cured it with herbs, so herbs cure it.' Name the promotion.
items.title: The Neighbor's Cure

items.correctExplanation: Yes — the policy is best because it's called best. The premise parrots the conclusion.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is circular reasoning. 'Best because best' travels nowhere.
items.lessonContent:
Circular reasons loop without landing anywhere.
Strip sentences: matching ends expose loops.
Real reasons import outside evidence.
Share this: straighten one loopy justification today.
items.question: 'This policy is best because it's the finest policy.' Name the loop.
items.title: The Finest Policy

items.correctExplanation: Right — potholes say nothing about library budgets. The herring reeks enough to steer attention.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is red herring. Streets and shelves share no logical road.
items.lessonContent:
Red herrings steer debates onto smellier roads.
Notice swerves: was the claim addressed?
Drag discussions back to the first question.
Share this: name the original topic mid-swerve.
items.question: 'Why fund libraries when potholes exist?' Name the drag.
items.title: The Pothole Swerve

items.correctExplanation: Correct — the sibling's snacks don't license yours. Charges need answers, not mirrors.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is tu quoque. 'You too' opens a second trial while yours waits.
items.lessonContent:
Mirrors defend nothing; they multiply trials.
Answer charges before filing counter-charges.
Hypocrisy-spotting proves zero about you.
Share this: answer one charge on its merits.
items.question: 'You ate snacks too!' says the caught snacker. Name the mirror.
items.title: The Snack Mirror

items.correctExplanation: Yes — the definition of 'gamer' shrank to expel the counterexample. Honest clubs admit exceptions.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is no true Scotsman. Disliking shooters can't revoke gaming membership.
items.lessonContent:
Shrinking definitions expel inconvenient members.
Real categories survive counterexamples.
Pin definitions before debates begin.
Share this: freeze one wriggling definition today.
items.question: 'No real gamer dislikes shooters,' says Dan, expelling dissenters. Name the shrink.
items.title: The Shrinking Clan

items.correctExplanation: Right — 'chemical-free' baptizes without testing. Nature brews poisons cheerfully.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is appeal to nature. Natural labels certify nothing about safety.
items.lessonContent:
'Natural' markets; it never measures.
Hemlock grows organically, after all.
Demand doses and trials, not adjectives.
Share this: dose-check one natural miracle.
items.question: 'Chemical-free, so completely safe!' Name the baptism.
items.title: The Pure Label

items.correctExplanation: Correct — coins keep no ledgers of past tails. Each toss starts history fresh.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is gambler's fallacy. Five tails oblige the sixth to nothing.
items.lessonContent:
Randomness owes nobody balance, ever.
Coins forget faster than gamblers.
Treat independent tosses as newborns.
Share this: free one coin from its 'debt'.
items.question: 'Five tails — heads must come now!' Name the debt.
items.title: The Owed Heads

items.correctExplanation: Yes — the hotspots were circled after the cases landed. Hindsight aims perfectly.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is Texas sharpshooter. Targets drawn after shots always bullseye.
items.lessonContent:
Hindsight draws bullseyes around bullet holes.
Predict first, then inspect hits.
Clusters bloom in pure noise constantly.
Share this: ask what was predicted beforehand.
items.question: 'Look how these cases cluster — the map proves it!' Name the painting.
items.title: The Circled Cluster

items.correctExplanation: Right — the word count doubled only after delivery. Shifting finishes rig the race.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is moving the goalposts. New targets after success confess rigging.
items.lessonContent:
Post-success rule changes confess rigged games.
Freeze finish lines before starting.
Fair judges grade agreed tests.
Share this: ink one finish line before work.
items.question: 'Five hundred words? Make it a thousand.' The demand doubles post-delivery. Name the shift.
items.title: The Doubled Demand

items.correctExplanation: Correct — believers carry evidence, never skeptics. Invisible dragons need visible proof.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is burden of proof reversal. Claimants prove; doubters merely doubt.
items.lessonContent:
Makers of claims carry the evidence uphill.
'Prove me wrong' dodges homework loudly.
Extraordinary pets need ordinary proof.
Share this: return one burden to its maker.
items.question: 'Prove my garage dragon DOESN'T exist!' Name the dodge.
items.title: The Garage Dragon

items.correctExplanation: Yes — untested means unknown, never effective. Gaps testify for nobody.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is appeal to ignorance. No research equals no knowledge either way.
items.lessonContent:
Gaps in knowledge endorse no products.
'Unstudied' confesses; it never certifies.
Wait for trials before wallets open.
Share this: shelve one untested wonder.
items.question: 'Unstudied, so it must work secretly!' Name the crowning.
items.title: The Secret Cure

items.correctExplanation: Right — featherweight bricks still stack heavy walls. Pieces never promise wholes.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is composition. Light parts build heavy totals routinely.
items.lessonContent:
Wholes surprise their lightest parts.
Cheap bricks raise dear houses.
Judge structures at structural scale.
Share this: weigh one whole against its parts.
items.question: 'Light bricks, so a light house!' Name the scaling.
items.title: The Feather House

items.correctExplanation: Correct — team speed describes averages, never every runner. Piles hide their grains.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is division. Fast teams shelter slow legs comfortably.
items.lessonContent:
Group speed never sprints every leg.
Averages cloak their weakest members.
Inspect parts before praising them.
Share this: split one team average today.
items.question: 'Fast team, so every runner is fast!' Name the scatter.
items.title: The Speedy Squad

items.correctExplanation: Yes — 'light' slides from weight to color mid-pitch. One word, two wallets.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is equivocation. Weight-light and color-light share spelling only.
items.lessonContent:
Sliding words bankrupt arguments quietly.
Pin each term to one meaning early.
Puns prove nothing, however pretty.
Share this: pin one slippery word mid-debate.
items.question: 'Light bags, light colors — all light!' Name the slide.
items.title: The Slippery Word

items.correctExplanation: Right — garage birth never tuned the guitar. Test instruments, not addresses.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is genetic fallacy. Garages birth legends and junk alike.
items.lessonContent:
Birthplaces never tune guitars or ideas.
Play the thing before judging the shed.
Origins narrate; tests decide.
Share this: test one garage-born thing fairly.
items.question: 'Garage-made guitar — must sound awful!' Name the judgment.
items.title: The Garage Guitar

items.correctExplanation: Correct — splitting arrival times equally serves nobody's facts. Compromise arbitrates interests, never clocks.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is middle ground. Halfway between claims lands on nobody's truth.
items.lessonContent:
Midpoints mediate deals, never facts.
Clocks don't compromise with wishes.
Reserve splits for interests alone.
Share this: refuse one factual fifty-fifty.
items.question: 'You say 8, I say 10 — meet at 9!' The clock says 8:40. Name the split.
items.title: The Split Clock

items.correctExplanation: Yes — bafflement measures the mind, never the mountain. Peaks ignore disbelief.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is personal incredulity. Inability to picture vast time dents nothing.
items.lessonContent:
Disbelief reports on believers, not mountains.
Deep time dwarfs every imagination.
Trade 'impossible' for 'show me'. 
Share this: marvel at one true immensity.
items.question: 'Mountains can't be THAT old — impossible!' Name the limit.
items.title: The Ancient Doubt

items.correctExplanation: Right — three five-star quotes frame; two hundred complaints crop out. Brochures curate, never confess.
items.incorrectExplanation: The answer is cherry-picking. Friendly quotes exhibit; full records decide.
items.lessonContent:
Curated quotes advertise; they never audit.
Demand denominators behind glowing excerpts.
Full records embarrass selective frames.
Share this: request full reviews behind one quote.
items.question: A ad shows three glowing reviews, hiding two hundred angry ones. Name the frame.
items.title: The Glowing Ad
